lessons.title: Introducing Yourself and Your Business
lessons.body:
In Spanish-speaking business settings, a proper introduction starts with a firm handshake and direct eye contact. Begin with "Buenos dÃ­as" (good morning) or "Buenas tardes" (good afternoon), then say "Me llamo [your name]" (My name is...). For your business, use "Soy el fundador de [business name]" (I am the founder of...) or "Trabajo con [business name]" (I work with...). If you're in agriculture, say "Nos dedicamos a la agricultura" (We are dedicated to agriculture).

Africans often have three names, so practice saying your full name slowly. Example: "Me llamo Amara Okonkwo. Soy de Nigeria. Mi empresa se llama Green Harvest y vendemos mango orgÃ¡nico a EspaÃ±a." (My name is Amara Okonkwo. I am from Nigeria. My company is called Green Harvest and we sell organic mango to Spain.) Notice the use of "se llama" for the company name.

When someone introduces themselves, respond with "Mucho gusto" (nice to meet you) or "Encantado/Encantada" (delighted). To ask about their business: "Â¿A quÃ© se dedica su empresa?" (What does your company do?). If they speak fast, say "MÃ¡s despacio, por favor" (Slower, please).

In many African cultures, we value relationship before business. In Spanish-speaking countries like Equatorial Guinea (where Spanish is official), they also appreciate a personal touch. So after the basics, add "Llevo cinco aÃ±os en este negocio" (I've been in this business for five years) or "Tenemos clientes en tres paÃ­ses" (We have clients in three countries). Numbers build credibility.

Practice with a partner: record yourself on your phone using the voice memo app. Listen for clear pronunciation of "ll" (sounds like 'y' in 'yes') and "Ã±" (sounds like 'ny' in 'canyon'). Repeat until you can introduce yourself in under 30 seconds. This is your elevator pitch in Spanish.

lessons.title: Small Talk with Other Entrepreneurs
lessons.body:
Small talk in Spanish business settings often revolves around family, travel, food, and football. Start with "Â¿CÃ³mo estÃ¡?" (How are you?) or "Â¿QuÃ© tal?" (How's it going?). A safe topic is the weather: "Hace mucho calor hoy, Â¿no?" (It's very hot today, right?). In Africa, we talk about rain and harvest; in Spanish, "la temporada de lluvias" (rainy season) is common.

Ask about their journey: "Â¿De dÃ³nde es usted?" (Where are you from?). If they say "Soy de Colombia," you can respond "He oÃ­do que el cafÃ© colombiano es excelente" (I've heard Colombian coffee is excellent). This shows you know their country. For Africans, mention "Me encantarÃ­a visitar [country] algÃºn dÃ­a" (I would love to visit [country] someday).

Food is a great connector. Say "La comida de mi paÃ­s es muy picante" (The food of my country is very spicy) or "Me encanta el arroz con pollo" (I love rice with chicken). Ask "Â¿CuÃ¡l es su plato tÃ­pico?" (What is your typical dish?). If they mention a dish you don't know, say "No conozco ese plato, Â¿cÃ³mo se prepara?" (I don't know that dish, how is it prepared?).

Football (soccer) is universal. "Â¿Le gusta el fÃºtbol?" (Do you like football?) works. In Spanish-speaking Africa, like Equatorial Guinea, they follow La Liga. You can say "Soy fanÃ¡tico del Barcelona" (I'm a Barcelona fan) or "Apoyo al Real Madrid" (I support Real Madrid). Avoid politics and religion until you know them better.

Useful phrases: "CuÃ©nteme mÃ¡s" (Tell me more), "Â¿Y usted?" (And you?), "Interesante" (Interesting). When you don't understand, say "No entiendo, Â¿puede repetir?" (I don't understand, can you repeat?). Practice with a friend: set a timer for 5 minutes and only speak Spanish about your day. This builds fluency for networking events.

lessons.title: Discussing Collaboration Opportunities
lessons.body:
When discussing collaboration, use clear, direct language. Start with "Me gustarÃ­a explorar una colaboraciÃ³n" (I would like to explore a collaboration). Then explain what you offer: "Nosotros podemos proporcionar [product/service]" (We can provide...). For example, "Podemos proporcionar cafÃ© de EtiopÃ­a" (We can provide coffee from Ethiopia).

Ask about their needs: "Â¿QuÃ© busca en un socio?" (What do you look for in a partner?). Listen for keywords like "distribuidor" (distributor), "inversor" (investor), "socio local" (local partner). If they say "Necesitamos un distribuidor en Ãfrica Occidental," respond "Tenemos contactos en Ghana y Nigeria" (We have contacts in Ghana and Nigeria).

Discuss terms carefully. Use numbers: "Podemos empezar con 100 unidades" (We can start with 100 units). Ask about timelines: "Â¿CuÃ¡ndo podrÃ­amos firmar un acuerdo?" (When could we sign an agreement?). If you need to think, say "Necesito consultarlo con mi equipo" (I need to consult with my team).

Common collaboration models: "joint venture" (empresa conjunta), "acuerdo de distribuciÃ³n" (distribution agreement), "franquicia" (franchise). For African businesses, highlight unique advantages: "Tenemos acceso al mercado de la SADC" (We have access to the SADC market). SADC is the Southern African Development Community.

Be prepared to talk about logistics: "Â¿CÃ³mo manejamos el envÃ­o?" (How do we handle shipping?). Mention Incoterms like FOB (Free on Board) or CIF (Cost, Insurance, Freight). If they use a term you don't know, ask "Â¿QuÃ© significa eso?" (What does that mean?).

End with next steps: "Le enviarÃ© una propuesta por correo electrÃ³nico" (I will send you a proposal by email). Or "Â¿Podemos agendar una videollamada?" (Can we schedule a video call?). Use tools like Google Meet or Zoom. Practice this dialogue with a colleague playing the other entrepreneur.

lessons.title: Attending Trade Fairs and Exhibitions
lessons.body:
At trade fairs, you need quick, effective Spanish. When you arrive at a booth, say "Buenos dÃ­as, Â¿puedo hacerle algunas preguntas?" (Good morning, can I ask you some questions?). If they say yes, start with "Â¿QuÃ© productos ofrece su empresa?" (What products does your company offer?).

If you are exhibiting, greet visitors: "Bienvenido a nuestro stand" (Welcome to our booth). Hand them a brochure and say "AquÃ­ tiene nuestro catÃ¡logo" (Here is our catalog). Ask "Â¿QuÃ© tipo de productos busca?" (What type of products are you looking for?). If they are interested, say "Podemos ofrecerle un precio especial para pedidos grandes" (We can offer you a special price for large orders).

Key phrases for trade fairs: "Â¿CuÃ¡l es su precio por unidad?" (What is your price per unit?), "Â¿CuÃ¡l es el pedido mÃ­nimo?" (What is the minimum order?), "Â¿Tienen representantes en Ãfrica?" (Do you have representatives in Africa?). Write down answers. Use a notebook or your phone's notes app.

Collect business cards. Say "Â¿Me puede dar su tarjeta?" (Can you give me your card?). If they don't have one, ask for their email: "Â¿CuÃ¡l es su correo electrÃ³nico?" (What is your email?). Repeat it back to confirm: "Entonces, es juan@empresa.com, Â¿verdad?" (So it's juan@empresa.com, right?).

Common trade fairs in Africa: "Feria Internacional de Dakar" (Dakar International Fair), "Feria de Lagos" (Lagos Fair). In Spanish-speaking countries: "Feria de Madrid" (Madrid Fair), "Expo Guadalajara" (Guadalajara Expo). Mention these to show you know the scene.

After the fair, follow up within 48 hours. Send an email: "Fue un placer conocerle en la feria. Adjunto nuestra presentaciÃ³n." (It was a pleasure meeting you at the fair. I attach our presentation.) Use a tool like Mailtrack to see if they opened it. Practice a 2-minute pitch in Spanish before the event.

lessons.title: Exchanging Contact Information and References
lessons.body:
Exchanging contact info in Spanish is straightforward. Say "Â¿Me permite su nÃºmero de telÃ©fono?" (May I have your phone number?). Or "Â¿Podemos intercambiar WhatsApp?" (Can we exchange WhatsApp?). WhatsApp is widely used in Africa and Latin America. If they agree, say "Mi nÃºmero es +234 801 234 5678" (My number is...). In Spanish, read numbers digit by digit: "dos, tres, cuatro..."

For email, say "Mi correo electrÃ³nico es amara@greenharvest.com" (My email is...). Spell it if needed: "a, m, a, r, a..." Use the Spanish alphabet: a, be, ce, che, de, e, efe, ge, hache, i, jota, ka, ele, eme, ene, eÃ±e, o, pe, cu, erre, ese, te, u, uve, doble uve, equis, ye, zeta. Practice spelling your name and email.

Ask for references: "Â¿Conoce a alguien que pueda recomendarme?" (Do you know someone who can recommend me?). Or "Â¿Puede ser mi referencia?" (Can you be my reference?). If they say yes, provide their name and contact to potential partners. In African business culture, personal references are powerful.

Useful phrases: "Le presento a mi socio, [name]" (Let me introduce my partner, ...). "Trabajamos con [company] en Kenia" (We work with ... in Kenya). "Puede contactar a [name] para mÃ¡s informaciÃ³n" (You can contact ... for more information).

Store contacts properly. In your phone, add a note: "Conocido en Feria de Dakar, interesado en cafÃ©." Use a CRM like HubSpot (free) or a simple Google Sheet. Follow up with a message: "Un placer conocerle. AquÃ­ estÃ¡ mi contacto." (Nice to meet you. Here is my contact.)

If someone gives you a reference, thank them: "Muchas gracias por la referencia." Then follow up with the referred person: "[Name] me sugiriÃ³ que hablara con usted." ( ... suggested I speak with you.) This opens doors. Practice this exchange with a friend until it feels natural.

lessons.title: Practice: Role-play a Networking Event
lessons.body:
Now put everything together. Find a partner (friend, colleague, or language exchange partner on Tandem or HelloTalk). Set up a mock networking event. One person plays an African entrepreneur (you), the other plays a Spanish-speaking investor or distributor. Use a timer: 10 minutes total.

Round 1: Introduction. Walk up, shake hands, and say: "Buenos dÃ­as, me llamo [name]. Soy de [country]. Mi empresa se llama [name] y nos dedicamos a [sector]." Then ask: "Â¿Y usted?" (And you?). Practice until smooth.

Round 2: Small talk. Talk about weather, food, or football. Use phrases like "Â¿De dÃ³nde es?" "Â¿Le gusta el fÃºtbol?" "Â¿CuÃ¡l es su plato tÃ­pico?" Keep it light. After 3 minutes, move to business.

Round 3: Collaboration. Say: "Me gustarÃ­a explorar una colaboraciÃ³n. Nosotros podemos proporcionar [product]. Â¿QuÃ© busca usted?" Discuss numbers, timelines, and next steps. Use "Â¿Le parece bien si...?" (Does it seem good to you if...?).

Round 4: Exchange contacts. Say: "Â¿Me permite su WhatsApp?" and "Â¿CuÃ¡l es su correo electrÃ³nico?" Write them down. Then say: "Le enviarÃ© una propuesta maÃ±ana." (I will send you a proposal tomorrow.)

After the role-play, review. Record it on your phone. Listen for mistakes. Common errors: using "tÃº" instead of "usted" (use "usted" for formal networking), forgetting to conjugate verbs, or speaking too fast. Correct them.

Repeat the role-play with different scenarios: one where you are the buyer, one where you are the seller. Use real numbers from your business. For example, "Vendemos 500 kg de cacao al mes" (We sell 500 kg of cocoa per month). This builds confidence.

Finally, create a cheat sheet with 10 key phrases and keep it in your pocket at real events. Practice 15 minutes daily for one week. You'll be ready to network in Spanish.
